title: TCP flags
description:
Decode a TCP header and describe the packet.

```
ports 51000 -> 443, seq 1000, ack 0, flags SYN, window 64240, header 20 bytes
ports 443 -> 51000, seq 5000, ack 1001, flags SYN ACK
ports 51000 -> 443, seq 1001, ack 5001, flags ACK
```
hints: The data offset is the top 4 bits of byte 12, in 32-bit words: `(p[12] >> 4) * 4` bytes (lesson 4.03).
Flags are byte 13: FIN is bit 0, SYN bit 1, RST bit 2, PSH bit 3, ACK bit 4, URG bit 5.
requirements: Read the ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, data offset, flags and window from the 20-byte header.
Print the names of all set flags (FIN, SYN, RST, PSH, ACK, URG).
Name the three packets of the handshake when you see them in order.
stretch: Detect a retransmission: the same sequence number seen twice from the same side.
